marks.gloss_en: the Sages: and a nap is as long as it takes to walk a hundred amot
Rav: a person may not sleep by day longer than a horse's sleep
Abaye: the Master's sleep is like Rav's
Abaye would sleep [by day] as long as it takes to go from Pumbedita to Bei Kuvei
R' Natan: one who goes to sleep by day may remove [his tefillin] or keep them on, as he wishes
(entertained) R' Yosei holds that one who has had an emission may not put on tefillin
one who forgot and had relations in tefillin grips neither the strap nor the box until he washes his hands, and then removes them
ומעשה נמי והביאו לו לרבן יוחנן בן זכאי ... העלום לסוכה -- the maaseh (of RYBZ and Rabban Gamliel) illustrates the stringency (kind svara: no support kind names a maaseh; header)
מעשה לסתור?! -- the mishnah permits casual eating outside the sukkah, yet its maaseh has RYBZ and Rabban Gamliel taking even a taste and two dates up to the sukkah
חסורי מחסרא והכי קתני: אם בא להחמיר על עצמו מחמיר ולית ביה משום יוהרא, ומעשה נמי ... (= p_machmir_al_atzmo): the maaseh illustrates a permitted stringency, not the law
the mishnah is lacunose and teaches thus: if one comes to be stringent on himself [and eat nothing outside the sukkah] he may be stringent, and there is no presumptuousness in it
they brought Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai a cooked dish to taste, and he said: take it up to the sukkah
when they gave R' Tzadok food less than an egg-bulk, he took it in a cloth
